item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Weaker. The 2024 record is dominated by election manipulation, throttled communications, protest crackdowns, and a collapse-in-exile ending rather than a resilient democratic handoff. The only counterevidence I found is reactive and narrow: a court order on job quotas and the later restoration of internet service after the protest wave ebbed.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Bangladesh: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-net/2024) — Freedom House, 2024.  
  Claim: Internet freedom in Bangladesh declined during the coverage period because the ruling Awami League manipulated the online information environment ahead of the January 2024 election, throttled internet and communications around BNP rallies, and then later imposed a nationwide shutdown and platform blocks during the July unrest. This is direct evidence that political freedom and democratic resilience were weaker by year-end.  
  Question IDs: `4B.10`, also `4B.9`, `4B.6`, `4B.5`, `4B.1`

- [Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/) — Reuters, July 20, 2024.  
  Claim: Reuters reported a nationwide curfew, internet/text shutdowns, and army deployment as the government escalated against protesters. That is strong evidence of a harsher and less resilient political environment than the one inherited.  
  Question IDs: `4B.10`, also `4B.9`, `4B.6`, `4B.3`, `4B.5`

- [Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) — Reuters, July 22, 2024.  
  Claim: Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence instead of moving toward compromise. This points to weaker democratic resilience and more coercive rule.  
  Question IDs: `4B.10`, also `4B.9`, `4B.3`, `4B.5`, `4B.8`

- [Bangladesh's crackdown left more than 170 dead, U.N. says](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) — United Nations / OHCHR, July 26, 2024.  
  Claim: The UN said more than 170 people had been killed and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity. This is strong external confirmation that the state response made the political environment less lawful and less resilient.  
  Question IDs: `4B.10`, also `4B.9`, `4B.6`, `4B.3`, `4B.5`

- [Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina resigns, interim government to be formed](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-pm-sheikh-hasina-resigns-interim-government-to-be-formed/2208572/) — Reuters, August 5, 2024.  
  Claim: Hasina resigned and fled after the crackdown, with an interim government announced after her departure. This shows 2024 ended in institutional collapse rather than stronger democratic resilience.  
  Question IDs: `4B.10`, also `4B.8`, `4B.5`

- [Exclusive-Bangladesh's Hasina did not resign before fleeing to Delhi, says son and adviser](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/exclusivebangladeshs-hasina-did-not-resign-before-fleeing-to-delhi-says-son-and-adviser-3565093) — Reuters, August 9, 2024.  
  Claim: Reuters reported that Hasina had not actually resigned before fleeing. That is direct evidence against an orderly democratic transfer and against stronger institutional resilience.  
  Question IDs: `4B.10`, also `4B.8`

**Weak Counterevidence**
- [Bangladesh restores internet as students call off jobquota protests](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-restores-internet-as-students-call-off-jobquota-protests-3540555) — Reuters, July 29, 2024.  
  Claim: Internet service was restored only after protesters called off the movement and conditions were said to be normalizing. This is the closest positive item, but it is reactive de-escalation after coercive disruption, not evidence of a stronger democratic order.  
  Question IDs: `4B.10`, also `4B.9`, `4B.6`

- [Bangladesh extends curfew ahead of court hearing on controversial job quotas](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-extends-curfew-ahead-of-court-hearing-on-controversial-job-quotas-3527975) — Reuters, July 21, 2024.  
  Claim: The Supreme Court scrapped most government-job quotas after protests had already escalated. This is the narrowest counterevidence on institutional constraint, but it was crisis-driven judicial intervention, not a sign that Hasina left democracy stronger.  
  Question IDs: `4B.10`, also `4B.4`, `4B.8`

**Search Gap**
- I found no reliable evidence that Hasina left Bangladesh’s political freedom or democratic resilience stronger than she inherited it.
- The limited positive items were reactive and conditional: a court ruling under pressure, and internet restoration after protests calmed. Neither shows durable improvement in freedoms or resilience.
